readme.text:
# Atom

> Atom and all repositories under Atom will be archived on December 15, 2022. Learn more in our [official announcement](https://github.blog/2022-06-08-sunsetting-atom/)

Atom is a hackable text editor for the 21st century, built on [Electron](https://github.com/electron/electron), and based on everything we love about our favorite editors. We designed it to be deeply customizable, but still approachable using the default configuration.

Visit [atom.io](https://atom.io) to learn more or visit the [Atom forum](https://github.com/atom/atom/discussions).

Follow [@AtomEditor](https://twitter.com/atomeditor) on Twitter for important
announcements.

This project adheres to the Contributor Covenant [code of conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
By participating, you are expected to uphold this code. Please report unacceptable behavior to atom@github.com.

## Documentation

If you want to read about using Atom or developing packages in Atom, the [Atom Flight Manual](https://flight-manual.atom.io) is free and available online. You can find the source to the manual in [atom/flight-manual.atom.io](https://github.com/atom/flight-manual.atom.io).

The [API reference](https://atom.io/docs/api) for developing packages is also documented on Atom.io.

## Installing

### Prerequisites
- [Git](https://git-scm.com)

### macOS

Download the latest [Atom release](https://github.com/atom/atom/releases/latest).

Atom will automatically update when a new release is available.

### Windows

Download the latest [Atom installer](https://github.com/atom/atom/releases/latest). `AtomSetup.exe` is 32-bit. For 64-bit systems, download `AtomSetup-x64.exe`.

Atom will automatically update when a new release is available.

You can also download `atom-windows.zip` (32-bit) or `atom-x64-windows.zip` (64-bit) from the [releases page](https://github.com/atom/atom/releases/latest).
The `.zip` version will not automatically update.

Using [Chocolatey](https://chocolatey.org)? Run `cinst Atom` to install the latest version of Atom.

### Linux

Atom is only available for 64-bit Linux systems.

Configure your distribution's package manager to install and update Atom by following the [Linux installation instructions](https://flight-manual.atom.io/getting-started/sections/installing-atom/#platform-linux) in the Flight Manual. You will also find instructions on how to install Atom's official Linux packages without using a package repository, though you will not get automatic updates after installing Atom this way.

#### Archive extraction

An archive is available for people who don't want to install `atom` as root.

This version enables you to install multiple Atom versions in parallel. It has been built on Ubuntu 64-bit,
but should be compatible with other Linux distributions.

1. Install dependencies (on Ubuntu):
```sh
sudo apt install git libasound2 libcurl4 libgbm1 libgcrypt20 libgtk-3-0 libnotify4 libnss3 libglib2.0-bin xdg-utils libx11-xcb1 libxcb-dri3-0 libxss1 libxtst6 libxkbfile1
```
2. Download `atom-amd64.tar.gz` from the [Atom releases page](https://github.com/atom/atom/releases/latest).
3. Run `tar xf atom-amd64.tar.gz` in the directory where you want to extract the Atom folder.
4. Launch Atom using the installed `atom` command from the newly extracted directory.

The Linux version does not currently automatically update so you will need to
repeat these steps to upgrade to future releases.

## Building

* [Linux](https://flight-manual.atom.io/hacking-atom/sections/hacking-on-atom-core/#platform-linux)
* [macOS](https://flight-manual.atom.io/hacking-atom/sections/hacking-on-atom-core/#platform-mac)
* [Windows](https://flight-manual.atom.io/hacking-atom/sections/hacking-on-atom-core/#platform-windows)

## Discussion

* Discuss Atom on [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/atom/atom/discussions)

## License

[MIT](https://github.com/atom/atom/blob/master/LICENSE.md)

When using the Atom or other GitHub logos, be sure to follow the [GitHub logo guidelines](https://github.com/logos).

notes: Commit cadence is measured over the latest 30 commits only.

causeOfDeath.headline: Internal sunsetting by its corporate progenitor in favor of a newer standard.
causeOfDeath.explanation: Despite being the pioneer of the Electron framework and amassing over 60,000 stars, Atom was officially decommissioned by GitHub. The final months of activity were dedicated almost exclusively to preparing users for the end, as seen in commit df229dd: 'Create new view to announce we're sunsetting Atom'.

timeOfDeath.note: The date of the final merge pull request before the repository was archived on December 15, 2022.

diagnosis.evidence: The official sunset announcement (2022-06-08) and the industry-wide shift toward VS Code rendered Atom's maintenance redundant for its parent company.
The package.json reveals a heavy reliance on coffee-script (2.8%) and older Node patterns that became increasingly difficult to maintain compared to TypeScript-based competitors.
While not a single person, the corporate 'solo' owner (GitHub) shifted resources away, leaving the project to drift at 1.2 commits per week before the final shutdown.

worthSaving: The Electron framework (which outlived its host)

marketToday.reasoning: The demand for extensible, web-tech-based editors is higher than ever, though the market is currently dominated by VS Code and new high-performance contenders like Zed.

autopsy.revivalScoreReason: The core community has already moved to forks like Pulsar, but the original codebase is too tied to legacy dependencies to revive as-is.
autopsy.epitaph: The 21st century arrived, and it brought a different editor.

newPositioning.oneLiner: The CSS-First Editor for Framer and Tailwind Power Users
newPositioning.targetUser: Frontend designers who build UIs directly in code
newPositioning.painPoint: VS Code is optimized for logic and TypeScript, not for visual styling and layout
newPositioning.whyNow: AI coding tools can now generate complex CSS instantly, but we lack a 'visual-first' sandbox.

keep: Electron core for deep CSS customization
kill: CoffeeScript — because it is unmaintainable in 2026
APM package manager — because npm/esm is the standard
Multi-language support — because we are narrowing to Web/CSS

crowdfundingPitch.title: Atom Redux: The Designer's Code Editor
crowdfundingPitch.story: I used Atom for years. It was the first editor that felt like it belonged to the web, but it died because it got slow and lost its way to VS Code. I'm bringing back that 'hackable' spirit, but with a narrow focus: being the best possible tool for design engineers. No more bloated plugins for backend languages we don't use. This is a lean, TypeScript-based rebuild that prioritizes CSS performance and visual feedback. I've stripped the legacy CoffeeScript and built a core that handles modern Tailwind and AI-driven design workflows. We aren't trying to be the best editor for everyone—just the best one for people who build the beautiful parts of the internet. This project is a return to the roots of what made Atom special: an editor that looks as good as the code you write in it.
fundingUse: Development of a high-performance Canvas-based renderer
Hosting for the community-driven CSS theme marketplace
crowdfundingPitch.backerReward: Founding Member badge in the editor footer and a vote on the 'Feature of the Month' roadmap.

resurrection.aiBuildPrompt: Build a modern, lightweight 'CSS-First' code editor in Electron. Use Vite, React, and TypeScript. The core feature is a split-screen layout: a Monaco Editor instance on the left and a live-updating HTML/CSS preview on the right. The editor must allow 'Meta-Styling'—where the user can open a CSS file that specifically targets the editor's own DOM classes to change its appearance in real-time. Do not include any backend language support; focus entirely on HTML, CSS, and Tailwind CSS. Include a command palette (Cmd+K) that allows users to toggle 'Inspect Mode' to select elements within the editor itself. Use a clean, minimal UI inspired by the original Atom 'One Dark' theme. Done means: the app launches, allows file editing, and reflects CSS changes in the preview pane instantly with no reload.
